do_not_use_when: The action is tentative or reversible.
No prior 888_JUDGE SEAL verdict exists for irreversible writes.
arifos_manifest.eureka_insight: History is immutable. A ledger without cryptographic permanence is just a suggestion.

mode_purpose.audit: Session-scoped audit package over sealed outcomes.
mode_purpose.changelog: Enumerate recent sealed changes for audit continuity.
mode_purpose.ledger: Read VAULT999 ledger tip / scoped entries (replaces phantom chain/list).
mode_purpose.seal: Anchor a payload to the immutable ledger.
mode_purpose.session_close: Close session continuity and emit terminal continuity receipt.
mode_purpose.verify: Cryptographically verify a prior vault entry.

purpose: Immutable ledger anchoring and cryptographic seal.
Writes terminal verdicts and audit events to VAULT999.
use_when: A terminal verdict needs to be made immutable.
An audit event must be cryptographically witnessed.

description: Append verified outcome or lesson to the immutable audit ledger. Requires ack_irreversible=true to confirm permanent commit. Outputs: immutable ledger entry receipt.

ack_irreversible.description: Set true to confirm you understand sealed entries are PERMANENT — they can never be edited or removed.

actor_id.description: Your agent identity, e.g. 'kimi-code/FI-008' or 'claude/sonnet'. Recorded in the audit log so this action is attributed to you.

actor_signature.description: Cryptographic signature over the request, if your agent holds a key — proves the call genuinely came from actor_id. Omit if you have no key.

constitutional.description: JSON block of governance metadata (floors consulted, chain references) — normally built by the kernel, not by callers.

constitutional_chain_id.description: Id of the evidence chain this call belongs to (observe→think→judge→seal). Copy it from the earlier step's response to link the steps together.

drift_events.description: JSON list of deviations observed, e.g. [{"what": "schema drift", "where": "tools/list"}] — stored with the record.

judge_state_hash.description: Hash string from the arif_judge SEAL response — ties this entry to the verdict that authorized it.

mode.description: 'seal' (default) — append a permanent entry; 'verify' — check one entry; 'ledger' — read the ledger head; 'changelog' — recent appends; 'audit' — integrity check; 'session_close' — close out a session into the ledger.

nonce.description: One-time random string (e.g. a UUID) making this request unique; protects against replay of the same call.

payload.description: The content to store forever, as a string (usually JSON-serialized) — the outcome, lesson, or record itself. Required for the write modes (seal, session_close); pure reads (verify, ledger, changelog, audit) may omit it.

seal_purpose.description: One sentence saying why this verdict/record must exist, e.g. 'closing deployment D-17'. Stored permanently alongside the record.

session_id.description: Session id returned by arif_init (looks like 'sess-…'). Pass it on every call after init so the action is attributed to your governed session.

session_token.description: Session Continuity Token (SCT) — the credential string arif_init returned alongside session_id. Pass it back on follow-up calls to prove the session is yours; without it the kernel treats you as unauthenticated.

witness_type.description: Who witnessed the sealed fact: 'ai', 'human', or 'external' system.
